Definition: from G575 and G3089; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce:--(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty.
BiblicalUsage: To free fully — to release, dismiss, or send away. Joseph, being a just man and not willing to make Mary a public example, was minded to put her away privily in Matthew 1:19, and Jesus teaches in Matthew 19:9 that whoever puts away his wife except for fornication commits adultery. Pilate released Barabbas unto the crowd in Luke 23:25 and delivered Jesus to their will, and the Roman examiners in Acts 28:18 would have let Paul go, because there was no cause of death in him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word shows how the same release can be just, cruel, or corrupt. Joseph's quiet release was mercy; Pilate's release of Barabbas was injustice wearing the robes of law; the Romans' willingness to release Paul was the truth finally being heard. Freedom is not always righteous — what matters is who is set free, and who pays for it.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Paul; Pontius Pilate
